items.review_rationale: Read degree of vertex in simple undirected graph by count of incident edges, preserving cardinality interpretation for potentially infinite graphs.

references.context: Edge e∈E with endpoint v, equivalently unordered pair containing v.

references.phrase: cardinality of set of incident edges
references.context: Number of edges incident to v, possibly an infinite cardinal.

references.disposition: The graph is simple and loopless, so each edge contributes at most one to degree of v.

items.review_rationale: Read simple graph vertex degree as cardinality of adjacent distinct neighbors and its coincidence with edge incidence in loopless graph.

references.context: Set of distinct u∈V such that edge {u,v} belongs to E.
Number of distinct neighbors of v, finite or potentially infinite.

references.phrase: degree counts neighbors only for simple graph
references.disposition: For multigraph with parallel edges, degree based on neighbor count can differ from incident-edge count.

items.review_rationale: Read closed metric ball with strictly positive radius and nonstrict distance bound from center, not necessarily a closed set in every arbitrary topology context outside metric topology.

references.context: Chosen center and positive real radius.

references.phrase: closed ball defined by weak inequality
references.disposition: This is the metric closed-ball set, not an assertion of equivalence with arbitrary closed subsets.

items.review_rationale: Read closed norm ball as all vectors at norm distance at most r from center in specified normed vector space, including positive radius and displacement v−a.

references.context: Norm of difference vector v−a in V.

references.phrase: closed norm ball of center and positive radius
references.context: Set of v∈V satisfying ∥v−a∥≤r with r>0.

references.disposition: Norm induces metric d(v,a)=∥v−a∥; this formulation depends on chosen norm.
